data.narrative:
Extropic, a Series A-stage semiconductors company founded by Guillaume Verdon and Trevor McCourt, has raised $50M+ to date. Valuation was triangulated using two applicable methods against a universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, including Rebellions, d-Matrix, Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $50M total raised proxy, implying a $100M valuation consistent with typical Series A advancement mechanics. Peer-median anchoring across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers—Rebellions ($2.3B Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A), and Positron AI ($1.0B Series B)—yields a $2.0B median with a $1.0B–$2.3B range. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (18.9x median across semiconductors) is not applicable due to absence of revenue disclosure.

These methods support a triangulated valuation range of $85M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide range reflects two competing narratives: a conservative stage-based floor versus elevated private peer valuations reflective of sector momentum. Key uncertainties include Extropic's revenue trajectory, technical differentiation relative to named peers, and capital efficiency relative to the $50M+ raised to date.
